title: Finite thickenings of a rational point and arbitrary base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be a section of its structure morphism. Separated means that the diagonal over $k$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $x$ is a closed immersion. Write $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to x_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (the stalk), and $\mathfrak m=\ker(R\to k)$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], local with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and has residue field $k$. For every integer $n\geq1$, the quotient $V_n=R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] is a nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and the closed subscheme $Z_n\subset X$ cut out by $\mathcal J^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}V_n$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $k$-scheme $T$, let $X_T=T\times_kX$, let $x_T:T\to X_T$ be the induced section, and let $\mathcal J_T$ be its ideal [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $\mathcal J_T=\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X_T}$ and the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal J_T^{n+1}$ is $T\times_k Z_n$. In particular for $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kV_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. These identifications are natural in $T$, compatible with $Z_n\hookrightarrow Z_{n+1}$ and $V_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow V_n$, and the latter maps are surjective.

source.place: Proposition 8.9 proof, printed p.150, first paragraph: finite local quotients and formation under extension of base. Explicit scheme formulation of that input. Infinitesimal neighbourhood construction and universal property: Stacks Tags 04EY (more-morphisms-definition-first-order-infinitesimal-neighbourhood) and 04EZ (more-morphisms-lemma-first-order-infinitesimal-neighbourhood), literature/stacks-project/more-morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] to the structure morphism and its section $x$. Thus $x$ is a closed immersion. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent. On any affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies this section with the quotient map $A\twoheadrightarrow k$; it is a $k$-algebra map because $x$ is a section. Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(A\to k)=\mathcal J(U)$. Its kernel is maximal, since its quotient is the field $k$.

A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and the whole ring, each generated by at most one element. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] a finite-type structure morphism is in particular locally of finite type, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $X$ locally Noetherian. By [pqf-def-locnoeth] choose the affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ in Step 1 with $A$ Noetherian. The germ map identifies $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $R$ Noetherian. The description in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] makes it local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR$. The map $R\to k$, $a/s\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$, has precisely this kernel and is onto since it fixes $k$. Thus $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$ and $R/\mathfrak m=k$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), with Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves) and Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and put $q=n+1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] with $C=R$, $K=\mathfrak m^q$ and $N=q$. Its hypotheses $\mathfrak m^q\subseteq K\subseteq\mathfrak m$ hold since $q\geq1$. It gives that $V_n$ is Artinian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^q$ and residue field $k$. Its Jacobson radical is this maximal ideal, since it is the intersection of the maximal ideals and there is just one. Apply the first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-finite-over-residue-finite] to $k\to V_n$: its quotient by that radical is the one-dimensional $k$-module $k$, so $V_n$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Finally $\mathfrak m^q\subseteq\mathfrak m\neq R$ ensures $V_n\neq0$.

source.place: Tags 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0), 00JB (lemma-artinian-finite-length), including its maximal-ideal filtration argument.

proof.text: By [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $\mathcal J^q$ is quasi-coherent and restricts on an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ to the ideal $\mathcal J(W)^q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] to construct $Z_n$ and identify its part over $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathcal J(W)^q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] its underlying subset is $V(\mathcal J(W)^q)=V(\mathcal J(W))$: a prime contains all $q$th powers of elements of an ideal exactly when it contains that ideal. These are the same subsets as for the original closed point. Consequently $|Z_n|=\{x\}$, so its inverse image of $U$ is all of $Z_n$, and $Z_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p^q)$ over $U$.

For $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ let $c=\bar s\in k^\times$ and $t=1-c^{-1}s\in\mathfrak p$. In $A/\mathfrak p^q$ the element $c^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}t^j$ is an inverse of $s$, since $s c^{-1}\sum t^j=(1-t)\sum t^j=1-t^q=1$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] extends $A\to A/\mathfrak p^q$ uniquely to $A_{\mathfrak p}\to A/\mathfrak p^q$. It kills $(\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p})^q$, because that ideal is generated by products of $q$ images from $\mathfrak p$. It therefore gives an inverse to the canonical map $A/\mathfrak p^q\to A_{\mathfrak p}/(\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p})^q$: the composites fix $A$, and the localized composite also fixes inverses of denominators. By [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] these are $k$-algebra maps. Together with Step 2 this identifies the ring in Step 4 with $V_n$. The forward map is the germ map followed by quotient, so the identification is independent of the affine neighbourhood: restriction to a smaller neighbourhood gives the same germ map. This yields the asserted canonical $\operatorname{Spec}V_n\hookrightarrow X$.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization); explicit finite geometric-series inverse in the rational-point situation of Milne Proposition 8.9, printed p.150.

proof.text: Let $g:X_T\to X$ be the projection. The square with $x_T:T\to X_T$ and $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is Cartesian: both fibre products represent a map to $T$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ agreeing over $k$, as follows directly from [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] first to $x$ and then to $Z_n\hookrightarrow X$. It gives $\mathcal J_T=\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X_T}$ and says that $X_T\times_XZ_n\hookrightarrow X_T$ has ideal $\mathcal J^q\mathcal O_{X_T}$. These statements use the image in the structure sheaf, with no injectivity assertion for the pulled-back ideal module and no flatness hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Tag 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion), part (1), including the ideal-image assertion.

proof.text: Let $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ be an affine open of $X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}D$ an affine open of $X_T$ with $g(V)\subseteq W$, so $g$ gives a ring map $C\to D$; such $V$ cover $X_T$, and every open of $X_T$ is covered by them. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and Step 4, $x^{-1}(W)\to W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathcal J(W))\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $Z_n\cap W\to W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathcal J(W)^q)\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ (if $x\notin W$ then $\mathcal J(W)=C$ and both are empty). By the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product], the part of $X_T\times_XZ_n$ over $V$ is $V\times_W(Z_n\cap W)$, and likewise for the section. [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_C C/\mathcal J(W)^q)$, the map to $V$ being induced by $d\mapsto d\otimes1$, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] identifies this $D$-algebra with $D/\mathcal J(W)^qD$. Hence, by the affine description in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], the ideal of $X_T\times_XZ_n\hookrightarrow X_T$, which Step 6 calls $\mathcal J^q\mathcal O_{X_T}$, has sections $\mathcal J(W)^qD$ on $V$; the same argument with $q=1$ gives $\mathcal J_T(V)=\mathcal J(W)D$. Extension of ideals commutes with powers: for a ring map $f:C\to D$ and an ideal $I\subseteq C$, both $(ID)^q$ and $I^qD$ are generated by the products $f(a_1)\cdots f(a_q)$ with $a_i\in I$, since coefficients from $D$ can be multiplied together. So by [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] $\mathcal J_T^q(V)=(\mathcal J(W)D)^q=\mathcal J(W)^qD$. Two subsheaves of $\mathcal O_{X_T}$ that agree on such a covering family of every open agree, so $\mathcal J_T^q=\mathcal J^q\mathcal O_{X_T}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], the closed scheme cut out by $\mathcal J_T^q$ is, over each such $V$, $\operatorname{Spec}(D/\mathcal J(W)^qD)\to V$, as is $X_T\times_XZ_n$. The identifications over $V$ are unique, because $D\to D/\mathcal J(W)^qD$ is surjective. So they glue, and the two closed schemes are canonically isomorphic over $X_T$. Pasting the two fibre-product conditions using [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $X_T\times_XZ_n=(T\times_kX)\times_XZ_n$ with $T\times_kZ_n$.

source.place: Tag 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion); Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product) for the affine charts; the affine ideal-product calculation underlying More on Morphisms Tag 04EY (definition-first-order-infinitesimal-neighbourhood).

proof.text: For $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $T\times_kZ_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kV_n)$. This identifies the projections with the canonical tensor inclusions. For any $k$-map $T_1\to T$, [def-pc-fibre-product] characterizes the induced map uniquely by its projections; all the identifications in Steps 6--7 commute with those projections, proving naturality for arbitrary $T$. Finally $\mathfrak m^{n+2}\subseteq\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ gives the quotient map $V_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow V_n$, $[r]\mapsto[r]$, which is onto by choosing the same representative. Likewise $\mathcal J^{n+2}\subseteq\mathcal J^{n+1}$ gives $Z_n\hookrightarrow Z_{n+1}$. On $U$ these are the maps $A/\mathfrak p^{n+2}\to A/\mathfrak p^{n+1}$, and their germ maps agree with the maps on $V_n$ because both send $[a]$ to its germ class. On an affine $T$ the base-changed transition is $b\otimes[r]\mapsto b\otimes[r]$ at the lower level, so it commutes with all these identifications; for general $T$ this equality holds on an affine cover and hence globally.
